test "an annotated tool's arguments are mirrored, unannotated ones are not", %{
      agent: agent,
      url: url
    } do
      respond_with(agent, tools_responder([@tool]))

      {:ok, client} = Client.start_link(transport: {HTTPClient, url: url})
      {:ok, _} = Client.list_tools(client)

      {:ok, _} =
        Client.call_tool(client, "test_custom_headers", %{
          "region" => "us-west1",
          "priority" => 42,
          "verbose" => false,
          "empty_val" => "",
          "non_ascii_val" => "Hello, 世界",
          "query" => "SELECT 1"

      headers = headers_of(agent, 1)

      assert headers["mcp-param-region"] == "us-west1"

      assert headers["mcp-name"] == "test_custom_headers"

test "a null argument omits its header", %{agent: agent, url: url} do
      respond_with(agent, tools_responder([@tool]))

      {:ok, _} =
        Client.call_tool(client, "test_custom_headers", %{
          "region" => "us-east1",
          "verbose" => nil
        })

      headers = headers_of(agent, 1)
      assert headers["mcp-param-region"] == "us-east1"
      refute Map.has_key?(headers, "mcp-param-verbose")
    end

findings.title: the NotObserved backfill is keyed by ID, not by name (Q4; listed for MES-158's upstream report)
findings.text: getChecks() pushes NotObserved FAILURE only for a declared id with NO emitted check. An id shared by several names (mirrors-designated-params: 6 names; base64-unsafe: 7; encode-values: 3) is satisfied by any sibling, so a client under which one name goes silently unemitted (for example, one that drops non_ascii_val from the arguments) passes the scenario with that check MISSING. Our adapter passes the context arguments verbatim, so the accepted run is unaffected (18/18, each name emitted once). An OC-side silence: not a null result, not a discount, no new disposition, and no A1.

findings.title: checkMcpNameHeader's raw !== emits nothing in this slice (negative)
findings.text: It is defined at byte 700442, inside the http-standard-headers class; the http-custom-headers class Ja spans 705563 (var Ja=class extends Ia{) to 714435 (},Ya=class extends Ia{). No check of this slice is emitted by it.

findings.title: over-encoding: ET is STRICTER than OC on the plain-as-is rows (Q5; the encoder is not changed)
findings.text: V3 (encode_value Base64s every value) leaves http-custom-headers 18/18 SUCCESS, because Ka compares a plain value's header after Wa DECODES it; the members asserting a plain value as-is go red (22 failures). The over-encoding is caught on the OC side only by Mcp-Name's raw !== in http-standard-headers (ClientMcpNameHeader_tools_call, _resources_read, _prompts_get FAILURE under V3), because Mcp-Name shares HeaderMirror.encode_value. It moves no disposition: V3 does not redden any of this slice's checks, so it is no row's limb.

findings.title: two violations are red in the harness only at ID grain (negatives, not used)
findings.text: V1 (no sentinel at all) and P2 (sentinel/1 raises on a newline) crash the client before the harness records a named check: NotObserved for 4 and 5 ids, no ClientCustomHeader_* name emitted. A row's named check is never red under them, so neither is a row limb (the crash limb reddens only at id grain). P2' (P2s) is the name-grain replacement.

findings.text: docs/conformance/oc-emitting-sites-2026-07-28.json, rung id_literal_site, records for ClientCustomHeader_Region, _EmptyVal, _Method and _InternalSpace the pushes of ClientCustomHeaderNoMirrorNumber [711090, 711556] and ClientCustomHeaderNoMirrorUnannotated [712511, 712909], where the id literal mirrors-designated-params occurs; those four names are emitted by checkParamHeader's push [714077, 714434], as the other ten ClientCustomHeader_* tokens are sited.
